Despite the outcome's name, mismatches include method, path, query, fingerprinted headers, and body bytes.

files.Title: Trellis.Mediator.TransactionalCommandBehavior<TMessage, TResponse>
files.Summary:
Pipeline behavior that automatically commits staged changes after a successful command handler.

The behavior wraps each command invocation in an scope, runs the handler (which stages changes via repositories), then calls if the handler returned success. If the handler returned a failure , no commit occurs and the staged changes are discarded when the underlying store/context is disposed.

Persist-on-failure outcomes. If the response implements and the per-instance flag is true (the canonical producer is ), the commit step also runs even though the result is a failure. This enables the worker-handler pattern of persisting a permanently_failed state row alongside the failure outcome. On commit failure for a persist-on-failure outcome, the commit error replaces the handler error in the returned result.

This behavior is constrained to messages — queries are not wrapped and incur no overhead.

Atomicity: the unit of work persists all staged changes within a single handler atomically (the shipped EF Core adapter does so through the DbContext's implicit transaction). Cross-aggregate operations that share the same unit of work are automatically transactional.

Nested-command semantics. When a command handler dispatches another command via IMediator, the inner command flows through the same pipeline and the inner opens a nested . The inner defers (returns success without touching the store) until the outermost scope unwinds. This prevents a successful inner command from committing a partially-completed outer command's staged changes. Caveat: if the inner command returns a failure but the outer handler ignores it and returns success, the outer's commit will persist any changes the inner staged before failing — handlers that need to discard inner failures' staged work must detach the affected entities themselves. Every implementation must implement with depth-aware semantics; the shipped EF Core unit of work does this with an internal depth counter.
